problems.description: In answer_main, `delivered = True` is set only after `print(deliver_answer(...))` returns. Two cases break the exactly-once guarantee after the text has already reached the pane. (a) A failure after the send succeeded: the print raises BrokenPipeError (an OSError), or Ctrl-C lands between the send and the flag. (b) A partial send: `herdr pane send-text` succeeds and `send-keys Enter` fails. In both cases the command says 'it did not reach the worker' and prints the retry commands.
problems.failure_scenario: Case (b): send-text types 'Use B' into the pane, then send-keys times out after its 15 s limit, raising CalledProcessError or TimeoutExpired. `answer` exits 1 and tells the operator to rerun. The rerun types the text again and presses Enter, so the worker receives 'Use BUse B'.
problems.fix: Set `delivered = True` right after deliver_answer returns, before printing. When send-text succeeded but send-keys failed, report that separately ('the text is typed in pane X but not submitted; press Enter there, do not rerun') instead of offering the retry commands.

problems.description: Nothing ever reconciles a `delivered: false` answer. Suppose the operator types the answer through `claude attach` without first running `answer --no-herdr`. The controller does record a pane answer while a question is waiting, but it ignores an answer that is recorded and undelivered, so the flag stays false. A later rerun of the printed command then types a second copy. If the worker has asked question 2 in the meantime, `undelivered_answer` looks only at questions[-1], so the rerun records the old text as the answer to question 2. The RUNBOOK warns against this, but the CLI's failure output does not.
problems.failure_scenario: The Herdr delivery fails. The operator attaches and types the answer, and the worker resumes and asks question 2. The operator then reruns the printed `answer RUN ui 'Use B'`. It records 'Use B' as the answer to question 2 and types it into the pane.
problems.fix: In wait_handoffs, when the row is `working` and the latest entry has `delivered is False`, set it to True under question_lock, the same way it detects a pane answer. Also add one line to the failure message: 'if you type it in the pane instead, do not rerun answer'.

problems.description: When the challenge checkout cannot be created, the new `blocked` event and the CLI output show only `Command '[git ... worktree add ...]' returned non-zero exit status 128.` Git's reason (for example 'already exists') is lost because challenge_worktree runs git with capture_output=True, so the operator has to rerun the git command to learn what to fix. Two other stretches of run_challenge are also still outside any `blocked` handler: the code between the checkout and the try (running marker, prompt file, print_command) and the code after it (pinned_digests, save_challenge). A disk error in either on `resume` leaves the re-pin's `running` as the challenge node's last status.
problems.failure_scenario: ChallengeCheckoutFails prints: Blocked: Command '['git', '-C', ..., 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', ..., '<sha>']' returned non-zero exit status 128. It does not say why.
problems.fix: In run_challenge's new except, append `error.stderr.strip()` when the error is a CalledProcessError that has stderr. This leaves challenge_worktree itself unchanged, which fix/worktree-lock owns. Optionally, widen the existing try so it starts before the running marker and ends after save_challenge.

problems.description: Merge risk with sibling branches. (1) fix/autoupdate replaces the challenge's Popen with popen_claude. For a missing binary, popen_claude waits out a real 60 s grace period (CLAUDE_MISSING_GRACE_SECONDS) and then raises TransientInfraError. After the merge, the missing-CLI subtest will therefore sleep 60 s and may see a different exit code or message. (2) The RUNBOOK answer paragraph (line 56) and the README Questions/export lines are edited by both this branch and fix/review-served, which will cause textual conflicts. (3) The contract text in server/projects.ts sits in fix/review-served's area. The hunks do not overlap, but the integrator should know.
problems.failure_scenario: After merging fix/autoupdate, ChallengeJobStops takes more than 60 s longer. If `start` maps TransientInfraError to exit 75, the `assertEqual(code, 1)` for missing-cli-001 fails.
problems.fix: The integrator should patch `workflow.sessions.CLAUDE_MISSING_GRACE_SECONDS` (or the sleep) in the missing-CLI subtest and align its expected exit code and message with fix/autoupdate's transient handling. Resolve the RUNBOOK line-56 conflict by keeping both edits.

problems.description: This was outside the assignment's reach, but the assignment names every node the challenge's events use. The 'Design challenge disabled' event is recorded under the node `controller`, and `controller` is a legal lane id that is in live use (portable-workflow-001, workflow-guardrails-001, and 4 committed feature files). The server's laneMap aliases a lane's own events to `launch_<lane>`, so with a `controller` lane this event, and every supervisor `controller` event such as `controller blocked`, attaches to launch_controller. `controller` cannot be reserved without breaking those runs, so the event node has to change instead.

problems.fix: Record the disabled event under CHALLENGE, which is left unattributed when the graph has no challenge node. Separately, report the broader clash between `controller` events and a `controller` lane (server laneMap) to the export/viewer owner.
